title: Film Industries Map and Cricket Basics
description: Two views. A schematic tile map of eleven language-based film industries in South Asia (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali in Kolkata, Bangla in Dhaka, Urdu and Punjabi in Pakistan, Nepali, Dzongkha and Sri Lankan cinema), each with its language, center and a landmark film with year; and an animated cricket over of 6 legal balls plus one wide, with runs adding up to 14 for 1 wicket.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Film and media
Popular culture
Cricket
Sports
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Explain that Bollywood is the Hindi-language industry in Mumbai and only one of many language-based film industries in South Asia.
Identify film industries in at least five South Asian countries and the languages they use.
Describe the structure of a cricket over: 6 legal balls, runs from running and boundaries, and wides that add a run but do not count as a ball.
prerequisites: Knowing that South Asia has many languages (Chapter 6)
keyQuestions: Why is Bollywood not the same as all Indian or South Asian film?
Why do Kolkata and Dhaka both have Bengali-language film industries?
What is an over, and why does a wide not count as one of its six balls?
misconceptions: Cricket is only an Indian sport.
Every delivery in an over counts as one of the six balls.
controls: Click or tap a film tile
